To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

competitive and cooperative learning styles were positively associated with mathematics achievement, and the relationship between competitive and cooperative learning and mathematics achievement were stronger in East Asian countries than in the USA.

competitive learning is a more effective strategy for improving mathematics performance for all four countries, while cooperative learning is more effective for the three East Asian top-performing countries than for the USA.

competitive and cooperative learning are positively related to mathematics performance for middle school students in the USA, Hong Kong, Japan, Korea, and that competitive and cooperative learners perform similarly in mathematics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how learning styles affect mathematics performance and how the relationship between learning style and performance is affected by culture.
the question of why East Asian countries have been so successful in mathematics education.
the question of why American middle school students perform so poorly in mathematics compared with their peers from the East Asia region.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relationship between competitive and cooperative learning styles and mathematics achievement in the three East-Asian countries is stronger than that in the USA.
the relationship between learning style and mathematics performance is not as strong as the one that exists between mathematics performance and the way that learning styles are practiced.

the way that competitive and cooperative learning styles are practiced and used by teachers in the USA may be different from the way they are used in East Asian countries and this may be a contributing factor to the differences between the two regions in mathematics performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
learning styles are a useful but limited tool for improving mathematics performance in the USA and East Asia.
the relationship between learning style and mathematics performance is not universal and that the relationship is dependent upon how different learning styles are implemented in different countries.
competitive learning is a better predictor of mathematics performance in the USA, while cooperative learning is a better one in the East Asian countries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
learning styles can be used to improve mathematics performance but only if teachers use them in the right ways.
the practice of learning styles should be tailored to the cultural and institutional context in which it is implemented.
the practice of both learning styles is important for students to develop effective mathematics learning skills and strategies.
